modified_caption: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output at a threshold of 1e-3 across various layers. The x-axis is labeled 'Layer,' and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 23, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled 'Sparsity Ratio,' and uses a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.8, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The blue dashed line, representing the sparsity ratio before the gate, starts at a ratio of approximately 0.0 at layer 0 and remains constant throughout. The green dash-dot line, representing the sparsity ratio after the average gate, begins at about 0.8 at layer 0 and decreases exponentially, reaching 0.05 at layer 5 and stabilizing near 0.0 from layer 10 onward. The orange dotted line, representing the sparsity ratio after the gate, shows a similar pattern to the green line, beginning at about 0.8 at layer 0 and decreasing to around 0.2 by layer 10, with a small spike after layer 20. Notably, the sparsity ratio after the average gate consistently exceeds the sparsity ratio after the gate across all layers.

modifications.claim: The green dash-dot line reaches 0.05 at layer 5 and stabilizes near 0.0 from layer 10 onward.
modifications.reality: The green dash-dot line reaches approximately 0.1 at layer 5 and stays close to 0.0 from about layer 10 onward, not 0.05.

modifications.claim: The sparsity ratio after the average gate consistently exceeds the sparsity ratio after the gate across all layers.
modifications.reality: The sparsity ratio after the average gate (green line) is consistently lower than the sparsity ratio after the gate (orange line) across all layers.

modifications.claim: The orange dotted line decreases to around 0.2 by layer 10.
modifications.reality: The orange dotted line decreases to approximately 0.15 by layer 10, not 0.2.
